Jīmūtavāhana
------------------------------------------
Jīmūtavāhana is one of the three most important writers of the धर्म-śāstras in Bengal, the other two being शूलपाणि (A.

-1580). He was a scion of the Pāribhadrīya ब्राह्मण family, had the title ‘Mahāmahopādhyāya’ and was the chief judge under the king विष्वक्सेन of Bengal.
Three works of his have come to light. They are: Vyavahāramātṛkā, Kālaviveka and Dāyabhāga.
The Vyavahāramātṛkā deals with judicial procedures like titles of law, fitness needed for appointing a person as a judge, different grades of courts, four stages of vyavahāra, divine and human proofs and so on.
The Kālaviveka discusses about the appropriate seasons and months for the performance of religious rites and duties and other allied subjects.
The Dāyabhāga is the most famous of his works. Matters concerning इन्हेरितन्चे, पर्तितिओन्, स्त्रीधन (a woman’s share and property), reunion and other related subjects are discussed in detail. There seem to be at least a dozen commentaries on this work.
See also DĀYABHĀGA.
The word ‘Jīmūtavāhana’ which literally means ‘one whose vehicle is the clouds’ is an epithet of god इन्द्र.
